topBuzzwords.definition: Landside = public area before security (check-in, arrivals hall). Airside = strictly secured operations area beyond security (gates, apron, taxiways, runways).
The designated paved area where aircraft park at designated stands to deboard, board, refuel, load baggage, and undergo ground servicing.

topBuzzwords.term: Get Off to a Flying Start
topBuzzwords.definition: Idiom meaning to begin an activity, project, or semester with immediate success, high momentum, and enthusiasm.
GPU (Ground Power Unit) = mobile ground generator supplying electricity at the gate. APU (Auxiliary Power Unit) = small gas turbine in the aircraft tail used when engines and GPU are off.
The organic passing of information, recommendations, or news from person to person through spoken conversation rather than formal advertising.
TRC = Turnaround Coordinator supervising ramp tasks between flight arrival and departure. AODB = Airport Operational Database managing flight schedules, gate changes, and allocated stands.
A traveler who refuses to follow crew instructions or behaves disruptively, risking flight diversions, police arrest, and heavy airline costs.
LCC = budget airline offering cheap baseline tickets. Ancillary Revenue = extra income from non-ticket sales (carry-on bags, seat selection, on-board meals).

grammarTrapsCaught.title: ❌ 'Luggages' and 'Trainings' do NOT exist!
grammarTrapsCaught.rule: Both 'luggage' and 'training' are uncountable nouns in English. Never add an 's'.
grammarTrapsCaught.correctExample: ✅ "We checked three pieces of luggage and completed our training course."

grammarTrapsCaught.title: 💡 'Used to do' vs. 'Be used to doing'
grammarTrapsCaught.rule: 'I used to work' expresses a past habit that is finished. 'I am used to working' means you are accustomed/familiar with it now.
grammarTrapsCaught.correctExample: ✅ "I used to live in Paris, but now I am used to living in Toulouse."

grammarTrapsCaught.title: ✈️ Apron vs. Taxiway vs. Runway
grammarTrapsCaught.rule: Exact spatial precision is required in operational briefings. Never refer to the runway when you mean parking on the apron or taxiing on taxiway Alpha.
grammarTrapsCaught.correctExample: ✅ "The aircraft pushed back from stand B4 onto the apron, taxied via Charlie, and lined up on Runway 14L."

grammarTrapsCaught.title: 🛫 Scheduled vs. Charter Flights & EU261
grammarTrapsCaught.rule: Scheduled = timetabled regular airline service. Charter = booked on-demand for a specific private or tour operator group. Passengers hold specific EU261 rights for severe delays.
grammarTrapsCaught.correctExample: ✅ "Our charter flight experienced a 4-hour technical delay at the stand, triggering duty of care obligations."

strengths: Rapid adoption of technical aerodrome terminology (Airside, Apron, Stands, GPU).
Engaging peer discussions on commercial dilemmas (alcohol on board, budget airline trade-offs).
Accurate understanding of passenger rights under EU261 delay rules.
growthAreas: Spoken Fluency: Eliminating pauses while searching for specialized English nouns.
Sentence Speed: Building complex cause-and-effect sentences without hesitation.
Distinguishing subtle pairs: Scheduled vs Charter flight, Delay vs Cancellation.
cohortReflections.feAdvice: Students agree that knowing exact physical zones of an airport (airside, apron, stands, taxiways) and ground jobs (TRC, aerodrome operator) is the single biggest factor to ace the 30-minute Formative Evaluation oral profile.
